title: Addresses and the verbs of `jig send`

kind.description: station for a station an address names, verb for a verb of jig send.

name.description: The station as an address writes it before its @, or the verb as jig send takes it after the address.

key.description: For a station, what its address's key is: item for the tracker's item key, pull-request for a pull request's number, none for a station whose address names the repository alone. Null for a verb.

stations.description: For a verb, the stations whose addresses take it, each separated from the next by a comma and a space. Null for a station.

person.description: For a verb, whether it is a person's command, which jig send refuses in a session the line started. Null for a station.

args.description: For a verb, the arguments it takes after the verb, as its usage names them; null for a verb that takes none, and for a station.

meaning.description: What holding the station means, or what sending the verb asks for.

values.name: pickup
values.meaning: The pick-up of a tracker item: held by the session that claimed the item to start its work

values.name: drive
values.meaning: The drive of a pull request: the driver that runs its review rounds, whether a dispatched re-arm or takeover or one armed by hand

values.name: followup
values.meaning: The follow-up of a merged pull request: the pass, a dispatcher's tick or a person's run, that settles what the merge still owes

values.name: steward
values.meaning: The steward of a repository: held by the judgment pass its owner host's dispatcher started for it, one at a time

values.name: assign
values.meaning: Hand the item to the line: assign it to the factory identity and, when it is in no dispatch state, move it into the first one, for the dispatcher's next tick to pick up

values.name: drive
values.meaning: Ask for a drive on a pull request that has none: the drive command label, which the dispatcher's next tick arms a drive for

values.name: rearm
values.meaning: Ask for a stopped drive to be re-armed in its existing working tree: a request bound to that stop and the rearm command label that the dispatcher reads

values.name: withdraw-rearm
values.meaning: Withdraw a pending re-arm request and remove its rearm command label

values.name: hold
values.meaning: Keep the line off a pull request with the hold command label, or keep a tracker item out of pickups and batches with a hold on its dispatcher host

values.name: release
values.meaning: Withdraw the pull request's hold label or the tracker item's hold on its dispatcher host

values.name: answer
values.meaning: Answer a parked question or a need's decision by approving or choosing one of its options, at any of these stations; a drive also takes the person's own words, and --all to approve every parked question it may at once, which the other stations refuse. The bracketed --decision and --decision-set can be left out only on a dry run and, for an individual answer, on a park framed without a digest: a real structured answer to a framed decision needs its digest, and a real --all approval needs the set token the dry run printed. One answer comment per item, read by the re-arm or the dispatcher's next tick

values.name: start
values.meaning: Ask the dispatcher of the host that owns the repository to start one steward pass on its next tick, whatever the judgment backlog holds: a request kept on that host, refused, with the rule named, while a steward pass holds the repository or the host's hourly steward budget is spent

values.name: pause
values.meaning: Pause a running drive at its next round boundary: a directive in the mailbox of the working tree that holds the drive on this machine

values.name: resume
values.meaning: Withdraw the mailbox directive it names, so the drive goes on past it

values.name: stop
values.meaning: Stop a running drive at its next round boundary: a mailbox directive

values.name: hold-push
values.meaning: Hold a running drive's pushes: a mailbox directive the driver checks before each push
